column1: # Game profile of Crash Bandicoot 4: It's About Time (Switch, update 1.2 = v131072)
# PEANUTS: a Peanuts Native profile (Banana Native has none for this title); whole file Peanuts' own
# Toys for Bob, Unreal Engine 4.25 (project name Lava), SDK 10.4.0, NVN, Wwise sound; subsdk0 is the movie module (NintendoSDK_movie).
# The shaders are in two shader code archives (ShaderArchive-Global-GLSL_SWITCH, ShaderArchive-Lava-GLSL_SWITCH) in pakchunk0-Switch.pak, a version 9 pak with a frozen index
# (dm/gfx/tools/uepak.py V9); every shader in them is an LZ4 block, decoded without the game's code.
# Status: provisional profile (dm/games/profile_guess.py from the survey), not run on a device from this profile yet; see README.md
# 60 fps (30 on the Switch): the game's config caps Unreal at 30. The host writes 60 into t.MaxFPS, 1 into rhi.SyncInterval and the frame time into r.DynamicRes.FrameTimeBudget
# (hle_fpslock.c; the rewriter finds the three variables by name, dm/tools/ue_cvar.py: main+0x7b0dea0, +0x79c5030, +0x7ae3330 in this build), so the game asks for present interval 1
# itself and its dynamic resolution sizes the picture for a 60 fps frame. Unreal steps the game by the time that really passed. The launcher's frame rate cap (30) keeps the Switch's rate

# Unreal: nninitStartup reserves a 62 GB address region and its FMallocBinned3 takes 37 GB of it, so a 64 GB alias region for the bring-up on the Mac. The rewriter cuts the allocator in any Unreal 4 / 5 main (dm/tools/ue_malloc.py) and gives the region what the alias region has room for (dm/tools/ue_region.py), so an iPhone takes a smaller guest block, as Octopath Traveler 0's profile (docs/reference/memory.md)
# the NPDM declares 80 MB of system resource
# the decoded shader code archives: the engine's global shaders and the game's material shaders
